scientific_significance: Direct observation of unconfined water table depth below surface. Primary measure of aquifer storage depletion.
Absolute hydrostatic head above mean sea level. Governs hydraulic gradient and regional flow direction.
Previous year pre-monsoon static water level. Strongest single predictor in annual time series (captures multi-year storage memory).
Multi-year autoregressive lags (t-2 to t-4). Captures multi-year cumulative drought or replenishment persistence in hard-rock aquifers.
4-year rolling mean depth. Represents localized base aquifer state smoothed of single-year monsoon anomalies.
4-year rolling standard deviation. Measures localized water table volatility and susceptibility to pumping stress.
Linear rate of depth change over prior 4 observations. Directly indicates whether aquifer is in steady state, depletion, or recovery.
Difference between pre-monsoon (drawdown) and post-monsoon (recharge) water levels. Core variable in GEC-2015 Water Table Fluctuation recharge calculus.
Fraction of aquifer volume that drains under gravity. Ranges from 0.015 to 0.03 for Karnataka weathered granites/gneisses. Essential for converting depth change to water volume.
Rate of water movement through porous matrix and fracture networks. Controls recharge dissipation and well yield.
karnataka_availability: Low to Medium (sparse point pumping tests)

scientific_significance: Product of hydraulic conductivity and saturated aquifer thickness. Measures aquifer transmission capacity.
Physical drilled depth of observation borehole. Establishes theoretical maximum drawdown limit before well runs dry.
Hydrogeological classification (Unconfined weathered granite, Fractured hard rock, Deccan basalt, Alluvial valley fill). Dictates recharge mechanism.
Total precipitation in hydrological year. Primary source of natural aquifer replenishment across Karnataka.
potential_data_source: IMD 0.25 deg gridded / KSNDMC district stations

scientific_significance: Cumulative precipitation during June-July-August-September. Accounts for 70-85% of annual recharge across Karnataka interior.
Cumulative precipitation during October-November-December. Critical for south-eastern Karnataka districts (Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru).
Cumulative rainfall over preceding 30, 60, and 90 days before pre-monsoon survey. Captures late summer or pre-monsoon shower infiltration.
Percentage departure from long-term normal rainfall (+/- %). Distinguishes meteorological drought years from average recharge years.
Multi-scalar meteorological drought index (SPI-3, SPI-6, SPI-12). Normalizes rainfall deficits across contrasting climatic zones.
potential_data_source: Derived from IMD gridded daily data

scientific_significance: Number of days with rainfall >= 2.5 mm. High intensity concentrated in few days yields high runoff and lower infiltration than distributed moderate rain.
Atmospheric evaporative demand calculated via FAO-56 Penman-Monteith. Directly drives vadose zone moisture depletion before groundwater recharge occurs.
Daily and seasonal air temperature. Governs vegetative water extraction and shallow soil moisture drying rates.
Clay, silt, and sand percentages in topsoil. Dictates surface infiltration rate (saturated hydraulic conductivity Ks) vs runoff generation.
Total depth of unconsolidated soil profile above bedrock. Governs soil water holding capacity before deep percolation reaches water table.
Surface elevation from satellite radar topography. Influences regional hydraulic potential and precipitation lapse rate.
Surface gradient. High slope (>10 deg) causes rapid storm runoff and minimal recharge; flat terrain (<2 deg) facilitates ponding and recharge.
ln(a / tan beta) index representing steady-state topographic wetness. Identifies recharge zones vs groundwater discharge depressions.
Total length of stream channels per unit watershed area. High density indicates impermeable bedrock and high surface runoff fraction.
Euclidean distance to perennial river, reservoir, or canal. Wells adjacent to surface water receive localized bank filtration and irrigation recharge.
Satellite optical vegetation vigor index. Serves as proxy for active irrigated cropping area and agricultural groundwater pumping.
Proportion of cropland, barren scrub, built-up urban, and forest. Cropland fraction correlates directly with agricultural borehole pumping intensity.
Annual volumetric groundwater withdrawal for irrigation, domestic, and industrial uses. Primary depletion driver in hard rock aquifers.
karnataka_availability: Medium (available as block totals every 1-2 years)

scientific_significance: Percentage of net sown area irrigated by tubewells/borewells vs canals and tanks. Directly indicates localized aquifer stress.
Ratio of gross annual draft to total annual replenishable recharge (GEC-2015). Categorizes blocks into Safe (<70%), Semi-Critical (70-90%), Critical (90-100%), Over-Exploited (>100%).
Kc * ET0. Total depth of water required to meet evapotranspiration of a specific crop without water limitation.
Fraction of total seasonal rainfall that enters soil profile and is stored in root zone for crop transpiration (FAO USDA-SCS method).
ETc - Peff. Net irrigation depth that must be supplied by groundwater pumping to avoid crop yield reduction.
Soil chemical properties governing crop salt and chemical tolerance. Determines whether specific crops (millets vs pulses vs sugarcane) are biologically viable.
potential_data_source: Soil Health Card (SHC) Portal / ICAR NBSS&LUP

scientific_significance: Days from sowing to harvest (e.g. Ragi: 105-120 days, Maize: 110-125 days, Red gram: 150-180 days). Must align with seasonal groundwater availability.
potential_data_source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) Bengaluru / Dharwad
karnataka_availability: High (officially documented in UAS crop packages)
